research:
I could not find the official 2026 seasonal factors or a consensus forecast for the September 19 week, so the estimates in section 4 are rough calculations of my own.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question settles on the first published value of FRED series ICNSA, which comes from the DOL weekly claims report. The figure for the week ending 2026-09-19 is due in the report of Thursday 2026-09-24, 8:30 ET.
- 2026-09-10: the latest report covered the week ending September 5. Seasonally adjusted (SA) initial claims were 206,000, down 1,000 from a revised 207,000. The 4-week average was 206,000. [DOL/govdelivery](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDOL/bulletins/4299777)
- 2026-09-10: the not seasonally adjusted (NSA) figure for the week ending September 5 was **176,567** according to the code-supplied FRED data. A search-engine summary of a DOL table gave 176,916, against 171,403 for August 29. I could not open the DOL release text: the DOL page returned 403 and the PDF could not be read. Treat roughly 176.6k as the starting level. [DOL PDF](https://oui.doleta.gov/press/2026/091026.pdf)
- The SA figure was 1,000 above the Bloomberg median of 205,000. [financecalendar](https://www.financecalendar.com/event/us-initial-jobless-claims-september-10-2026/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value is first published on 2026-09-24. Before that, the 2026-09-17 report (week ending September 12, which includes Labor Day) will update the trend.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: SA claims held at 206k, with continuing claims at 1.774M for the week ending August 29. The NSA insured unemployment rate was 1.0%. The largest state increases were Michigan (+2,075, manufacturing layoffs) and California (+1,967). [verifiedinvesting](https://verifiedinvesting.com/blogs/us-economic-metrics/jobless-claims-week-ending-september-5-2026), [search summary of DOL](https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf)
- Summer 2026: claims stayed historically low, with the 4-week average near 204k in mid-August. [financecalendar](https://www.financecalendar.com/weekly-jobless-claims/)
- Recent NSA weeks in 2026: July 25: 176,535; August 1: 172,472; August 8: 189,203; August 15: 173,017; August 22: 170,596; August 29: 171,403. These are current, possibly revised, FRED values. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/ICNSA)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
Mid-September is near the seasonal low for NSA claims. Labor Day falls on September 7 in 2026, so:
- the week ending September 12 contains the holiday;
- the target week ending September 19 is the week after the holiday week.

NSA values in past years, lined up by the holiday ("pre-holiday week" to "week after the holiday week"):

| Year | Labor Day | Pre-holiday week | Week after holiday week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | Sept 1 | Aug 30: 196,712 | Sept 13: 195,433 | -0.6% |
| 2024 | Sept 2 | Aug 31: 190,623 | Sept 14: 186,832 | -2.0% |
| 2023 | Sept 4 | Sept 2: 191,353 | Sept 16: 176,586 | -7.7% |
| 2022 | Sept 5 | Sept 3: 172,835 | Sept 17: 168,702 | -2.4% |
| 2021 | Sept 6 | Sept 4: 285,683 | Sept 18: 306,581 | +7.3% (pandemic noise) |

[FRED ICNSA](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/ICNSA.txt). The 2025 figures were inflated by fraudulent claims in Texas.

- **Applying the 2022-2025 changes to 176,567** gives about 163.0k to 175.5k, with a median near 172-173k.
- **Lining up by calendar date** (the week ending near September 6-10 to two weeks later) instead gives:
  - 2025: -11.7%
  - 2024: -1.7%
  - 2023: 0.0%
  - 2022: +0.8%
- **Implied seasonal factors** (my own calculation, NSA divided by first-print SA):
  - Week ending September 5, 2026: about 0.857.
  - Week after the holiday week: about 0.846 in 2025 and 0.853 in 2024.
  - Late-September weeks: about 0.83 in 2024 and 2025.
  - If SA claims stay near 206k, factors of 0.83-0.85 imply roughly **171k-175k** NSA.
- **Year-over-year**: 2026 is running well below 2024-2025 (about 177k versus 196-205k in the comparable early-September weeks) and close to 2023 levels.
- **Statistical baseline** (from your code, not seasonal): p25 162k, p50 176k, p75 191k. That spread is wider than the seasonal patterns above suggest.
- **Typical noise**: week-to-week NSA moves of ±5-10k are common in August and September (for example, 2026 NSA went 172k, then 189k, then 173k in early August).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market and no economist consensus for the NSA figure for the week ending September 19.
- SA consensus forecasts usually come out in the week of release. The most recent was 205k for the week ending September 5.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-17: the DOL report for the week ending September 12 (the Labor Day week). It is usually low NSA because of the holiday, and it will also revise the September 5 figure.
- 2026-09-24: the DOL report that publishes the value this question resolves on.
- Possible shocks:
  - State layoffs: Michigan manufacturing was flagged in the latest report.
  - Hurricane season: storms in the Gulf or Southeast could push claims up in affected states. I did not check the current tropical outlook.
  - Fraud spikes like the Texas episode in 2025.
  - Any federal funding or shutdown developments around the end of the fiscal year on September 30.
